narrative:
Based on the analysis of your academic profile, the model estimates an 80% likelihood that you will fail your final year. Since this exceeds the 10% threshold, you are required to enroll in remedial courses.

The single strongest factor driving this prediction is your history of past academic failures. Unlike students who are not required to take remedial courses, who on average have no prior failures, you have experienced one failed class. This significantly increases the concern about your ability to successfully complete the final year without additional support.

The second most influential factor relates to your mother's level of education. While half of students not required to take remedial courses have mothers with higher education, your mother completed only primary education. Research consistently shows that parental educational background can affect the academic support available at home, and in your case this further contributed to the prediction of risk.

There is, however, one encouraging signal in your profile. Your strong desire to pursue higher education works in your favor, pushing the prediction slightly toward passing. This motivation is something you should hold onto and actively build upon.

Given these findings, the remedial courses are designed specifically to address the academic gaps that may have contributed to your previous failure and to strengthen your foundation before the final year. You are encouraged to make full use of the additional support provided, speak with your teachers or academic advisor about targeted study strategies, and remember that your ambition for higher education is a genuine asset. With the right support, improving your outcome is entirely achievable.
